objective:
Repository support for subject + action tags on top of schema v2 (TG2.1, ADR-040): load the tag catalog, and save an entry under a subject tag and an action tag in one transaction. Background: each entry gets a SUBJECT tag (what it was done to: furnace, hot tub) and an ACTION tag (what was done: change filter, mow) plus an optional duration. The AI only extracts words; pure core-domain logic (`tagging`: TagCatalog/KnownTag/KnownPair/TagKind, TagNormalizer, TagResolver, TagDecisionPolicy) decides AUTO_SAVE / CONFIRM / NEEDS_REVIEW. Schema v2 (ADR-040): tables subjects / actions (status TagStatus ACTIVE|MERGED, normalized_name = TagNormalizer.key, not unique in the schema), subject_aliases / action_aliases (unique per tag + normalized_alias, AliasSource), canonical_activities = the PAIR with nullable subject_id / action_id (unique together), occurrences.duration_seconds, interpretations.extracted_subject / extracted_action / duration_expression / resolved_duration_seconds, corrections.previous/new_duration_seconds. The capture pipeline is NOT switched in this task (Stage 3); the existing v3 path must behave exactly as before.

DOMAIN API (core-domain `repository` package, new file TagRepository.kt; KDoc in the same style and error contract as ActivityRepository):
- `sealed interface TagTarget { data class Existing(val tagId: String); data class New(val displayName: String) }`.
- `data class TaggedAcceptRequest(captureId, interpretation: InterpretationRecord, subject: TagTarget, action: TagTarget, occurredAt: Instant, timePrecision: TimePrecision, activityState: ActivityState, durationSeconds: Long?, learnSubjectAlias: String? = null, learnActionAlias: String? = null)`.
- `interface TagRepository { suspend fun loadTagCatalog(): TagCatalog; suspend fun acceptTagged(request: TaggedAcceptRequest): String }` and `interface LedgerRepository : ActivityRepository, TagRepository`.
- `InterpretationRecord` (core-domain interpretation package) gains `extractedSubject: String? = null, extractedAction: String? = null, durationExpression: String? = null, resolvedDurationSeconds: Long? = null` (defaults, placed last, so every existing caller compiles unchanged); the data layer stores them in the v2 columns for BOTH accept paths and recordOutcome (null for v3 callers).
- Views gain fields with null defaults, placed last: `OccurrenceView.durationSeconds`, `ActivityView.subjectId` / `actionId`, `HistoryOccurrence.subjectName` / `actionName` / `durationSeconds` (current display names of the pair's tags, null for untagged pairs). loadHistory stays ONE statement (join subjects/actions).

SEMANTICS of acceptTagged (one database transaction; nothing written on any error):
1. Idempotent per capture: if the capture already has an occurrence, return its id and write NOTHING (no tags, aliases, interpretation).
2. Resolve each target against tags OF ITS OWN KIND. Existing(id): must exist and be ACTIVE, else IllegalArgumentException (a MERGED tag is refused; the caller re-resolves). New(name): key = TagNormalizer.key(name); blank key -> IllegalArgumentException; if an ACTIVE tag of that kind has normalized_name == key, reuse it (oldest created_at, then lowest id, if several), else if an ACTIVE tag of that kind has an alias with that key, reuse that tag (same tie-break), else insert a new ACTIVE tag with display_name = the given name trimmed, normalized_name = key. This makes concurrent captures ('Wi-Fi' then 'WiFi') converge instead of creating duplicates; it is data integrity, not product policy.
3. Pair: the canonical_activities row with that (subject_id, action_id); if it exists and is ACTIVE use it; if it exists and is not ACTIVE -> IllegalArgumentException; else insert an ACTIVE pair with both ids, display_name = "<subject display> <action display>"-style label of your choosing (document it; it is a cache for legacy screens -- history reads the tag names), normalized_name via the existing NameNormalizer, merged_into null.
4. Insert the interpretation (incl. extraction fields), the occurrence (duration_seconds = request.durationSeconds, must be null or >= 0 else IllegalArgumentException), set the capture PERSISTED -- same rules and ordering guarantees as acceptInterpretation (interpretation must name this capture; unknown capture -> IllegalArgumentException).
5. Alias learning (used when the user accepts a 'did you mean X?' card): for learnSubjectAlias / learnActionAlias when non-null: key = TagNormalizer.key(text); skip when blank, equal to the final tag's normalized_name, or already an alias key of that tag; otherwise insert an alias (alias_text trimmed, source AliasSource.AI_CONFIRMED). Never fails the save because an alias is redundant.
6. Every write goes through the LedgerWriteDao pattern: a new `@Transaction open fun acceptTagged(...)` with `protected abstract` primitives (inserts with default ABORT; reads by id / key); no @Update/@Upsert/@Delete/REPLACE/DELETE anywhere; extend DaoWriteSurfaceGuardTest accordingly. Expose through ActivityLedgerWriter like the existing operations. SQLiteConstraintException is translated to IllegalArgumentException by the repository, as today.

loadTagCatalog: TagCatalog(subjects = ACTIVE subjects as KnownTag(kind SUBJECT, displayName, aliases = alias_text list oldest first), actions likewise, pairs = KnownPair for every ACTIVE canonical activity whose subject_id AND action_id are both non-null AND both tags ACTIVE). Bounded number of queries (no per-row query). Deterministic order (by normalized_name, id).

Wiring: RoomActivityRepository implements LedgerRepository; `createActivityRepository(context, clock)` returns LedgerRepository (source-compatible for existing callers). Do NOT change app-phone/app-wear code; they must still compile and pass. Do NOT change the in-memory fake in core-testing (Stage 3 adds tag support to it if needed) -- it implements ActivityRepository only and must still compile.

TESTS (core-data, Robolectric, in the style of RoomActivityRepositoryTest): empty catalog -> empty TagCatalog; New+New creates both tags + pair + occurrence and the catalog then contains them and the pair; second capture with Existing ids reuses the pair (one canonical activity); New 'Wi-Fi' after existing 'WiFi' reuses it; New whose key matches an alias reuses that tag; New subject equal to an existing ACTION name creates a separate SUBJECT (kinds never mix); idempotent second call writes nothing (row counts unchanged, even with different targets/aliases); unknown or MERGED Existing id, blank New name, negative duration, unknown capture, interpretation for another capture -> IllegalArgumentException and NOTHING written (including no new tag created by the other target -- prove rollback); alias learning: inserted when different, skipped when equal to name key / existing alias / blank; extraction fields and duration round-trip (interpretation row, OccurrenceView, HistoryOccurrence with tag names); history of a v3 (untagged) entry has null tag fields; loadTagCatalog excludes MERGED tags (insert one via raw SQL fixture), untagged pairs and pairs with a MERGED tag; existing v3 tests unchanged and passing.

DOCS: docs/DATA_MODEL.md -- a short subsection on how a tagged entry is written (find-or-create tags and pair, convergence rule, alias learning source). docs/DECISIONS.md -- append a dated 'Amendment (TG2.2)' to ADR-040 stating the New-name convergence rule and the AI_CONFIRMED alias source. No other doc changes.

RULES: no product policy in the repository beyond the data-integrity rules above (no fuzzy matching, no TagResolver call in the data layer); raw captures never modified except processing_state; no logging; exception messages carry ids and enum names only, never tag names or text.
non_goals: No corrections / alias learning from corrections (TG2.3), no rename/merge (TG2.4).
No pipeline, UI, watch or core-ai change; the v3 path is untouched.
No schema change (v2 is fixed by TG2.1); if you believe one is needed, report scope_change_requested.
No in-memory fake changes in core-testing.
acceptance_criteria: TagTarget, TaggedAcceptRequest, TagRepository and LedgerRepository exist in core-domain with KDoc'd error contracts; InterpretationRecord and the views gain the new nullable fields with defaults; all existing callers and fakes compile unchanged.

acceptTagged implements semantics 1-6 in one transaction through a new LedgerWriteDao @Transaction operation; the write-surface guard covers it and passes; errors write nothing (rollback proven by tests).
loadTagCatalog returns exactly ACTIVE tags with aliases and pairs whose two tags are both ACTIVE, in deterministic order, with a bounded number of queries.
History and occurrence views carry tag names and duration; loadHistory is still one statement; v3 entries show null tag fields.
Every test listed in the packet exists and passes; all existing core-domain, core-data, core-testing and app-phone tests pass; no schema file or entity changed.
DATA_MODEL.md subsection and ADR-040 amendment written; no forbidden path changed.
